_README: map_sn.json — the emit_matrix.py config for SharkNinja (NYSE: SN).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED TEMPLATE. SN is NOT yet in BBG_CONSENSUS.txt (as of Sep 2026 that file
carries eight tickers: AMZN, GOOGL, LYFT, META, NVDA, SPOT, TBBB, UBER). Adding it is a
Bloomberg-terminal job for San or Oscar - nothing in this repo can work around it.
The `codes` below are the Bloomberg field names this desk EXPECTS SharkNinja to use, written
from the metric set already in js/results-data/sn.js. They are a starting point, NOT verified
against an export. Codes differ per ticker (AMZN's operating income is IS_COMPARABLE_EBIT,
LYFT's is IS_EBIT_AS_REPORTED), so they MUST be checked before the first real run.
THE ORDER OF WORK once SN's row exists in the txt:
1. py inspect_matrix.py SN
Prints every slot with its code, segment, scale and populated horizons. Correct the
`code` values below off its CODE column, and DELETE any metric it does not carry.
A wrong code yields an almost-empty matrix rather than an error - that is why step 1
is not optional.
2. Read the `scale` column while you are there. A blank scale on a money row means WHOLE
UNITS, not millions. Declare the target unit here and the generator normalizes.
3. SUMMIT_DOCS="G:/My Drive/Summit/Docs/0" py emit_matrix.py SN map_sn.json
Check the resolution report (every metric must bind to a slot, none UNRESOLVED) and
the frozen-series check (a real consensus never reprints a value to four decimals;
anything flagged goes in `drop` until Bloomberg fixes the cell).
4. py verify_preprint.py SN
The acceptance test. `blanked` must be 0 - the matrix ADDS to the dataset and must
never silently subtract from it.
5. py apply_matrix.py SN
Splices estMatrix into js/results-data/sn.js. Idempotent; re-running replaces the
block wholesale and touches nothing hand-written.
WHAT THIS UNLOCKS, automatically, with no further code:
- Evolution > Estimates renders (the engine gates that pane on `estMatrix`/`evolution`).
- The vintage picker and the as-of axis appear on Results.
- Evolution > Earnings swaps its pending notice for the real Setup grid and scorecard.
STILL NOT UNLOCKED by this file: the Summit half of estMatrix and the `evolution` block both
come from Summit MCP snapshots (emit_summit_matrix.py / emit_evolution.py), and there is no
Summit DCF model for SN. Until one exists the Summit line stays null and no surprise
scorecard against the model is possible. See docs/RESULTS_CONVENTIONS.md section 8.3.
KPI AUTHORIZATION: whatever the txt turns out to carry for SN is THE valid set for the Setup
grid and the charts (EARNINGS_CONVENTIONS section 5 rule 6). js/results-data/sn-setup.js
currently exposes every line in snResults because there is no authorized set to gate against
yet - re-check it against metric1..9 + metric_kpi1..N here and drop anything unauthorized.

rev.label: Net sales
rev._note: Total reported net sales. Highest-confidence guess - this code is near-universal.

opIncome.label: Operating income
opIncome._note: VERIFY FIRST - this is the code that differs most between tickers.

ebitdaAdj.label: Adjusted EBITDA
ebitdaAdj._note: The line SharkNinja itself guides. If the txt carries only a GAAP EBITDA, map that to ebitdaGaap instead and leave this unresolved rather than substituting.

epsAdj.label: Adjusted diluted EPS
epsAdj._note: The headline line for SN - its FY guidance is given as Adjusted Net Income per diluted share.

sm.label: Selling & Marketing expense
sm._note: SN splits S&M and G&A; Bloomberg may carry only a combined SG&A. If so, drop both rather than mapping a combined figure onto one of them.

_note: SN reports ONE segment, so there are no segment-level consensus lines to expect.
Bloomberg may still carry its own category or brand estimates. If inspect_matrix.py shows
them, map them to the EXISTING dataset keys so the Results tab does not grow a parallel
set: segCleaning, segCookBev, segFoodPrep, segBeautyHome, regionNA, regionIntl,
brandShark, brandNinja. Do not invent new keys.

_drop_note: Series the frozen-series check flags go here, with a one-line reason and the date, until the Bloomberg cell is fixed. A frozen series reads as a beautifully smooth estimate and is entirely fictional - see the README.
